title: Trace-Reconstruction Attacks and Trace-Private Defenses for Confidential LLM Agents
evidence_status: Headline values come from the Azure matrix journals in this repository (artifacts/matrix-baseline.jsonl for the main arms, matrix-{autonomy,architecture,model}.jsonl for the generality sweep, utility-azure.jsonl for the judged utility study) and regenerate via `make paper-all`. Both journal sets are provenance tier live_replication -- a real provider rather than the deterministic fixture -- which is the label the generator refuses to apply to fixture output. The superseded gpt-4o-mini journals (artifacts/experiment-usenix26-main.jsonl, artifacts/experiment-usenix26-gen.jsonl, artifacts/utility-usenix26.jsonl) remain tracked and analysable -- CI asserts it -- and supply the weak-vs-strong comparison values under a 'hist' prefix. WHERE THE RUNS EXECUTED, stated in detail because an earlier version of this field got it wrong in both directions. The headline arm was re-run in full INSIDE the attested Azure SEV-SNP confidential VM (artifacts/matrix-cvm.jsonl), cell for cell at the same seed, the same crew deployments and the same corpus digest as the host baseline, using the CI-published container image with no file copied in after boot -- each row names the producing commit in provenance.source_revision. Every row in that journal carries provenance.attestation with verdict='verified', hardware_backed=true, maa_verified=true, tee_type='sevsnpvm', the launch measurement in the clear, and an azure-vtpm-ak-quote-v1 key binding; the MAA token and the JWKS snapshot fetched at run time live in artifacts/matrix-cvm.attestation.json, and each row references its epoch by digest so a reader can tell which evidence covers which row. The run refuses to start without that binding (--require-attestation). The GENERALITY SWEEP is different and is counted separately: matrix-{autonomy,architecture,model}.jsonl ran on the artifact host against the same Azure deployments, and those journals carry attestation provenance recording verdict='simulated' with hardware_backed=false -- the honest-degradation invariant exercised by one code path producing two truthful answers, which is the whole reason the two journals are worth shipping side by side. What the in-CVM arm does NOT establish, and the manuscript says so: the trace features are recorded by the guest's own runtime, so the timing is application-level and a real host would see strictly more; the model is not in the enclave, since every crew step crosses to a commercial API over TLS; and the chain bounds where the signing key ran, not whether it was honest -- the key is proven resident in the attested guest, not proven to have been generated there. This file remains the transcription-of-record for the checked-in PDF/LaTeX and is hash-anchored to both; its numeric sections are generated by scripts/sync_paper_reference.py.

Superseded by the calibrated-null revision. Unlike the previous entry this is a genuine content change, not a rebuild: the membership claim was restated (see membership_revision below), the full-pad column and the deadline-overrun figures became measured rather than asserted, both figures became generated artifacts derived from the archived journal, and the latency prose was corrected to say the harness sleeps to the deadline (which it does) rather than modelling the cost.

Superseded by the finite-epsilon partition correction and the ordinal statistics. The frontier's template partition was derived from empirical tertiles of the observed depths, which on this workload collapsed both boundaries onto 3.0: only two of the three templates were ever occupied, so the table reported K=3 keep probabilities for a mechanism that could not emit three templates. The partition is now derived from the published plan depth range, which is data-independent as a public template set must be.

Superseded by two changes, both of which remove a way the manuscript could state something the tree does not support. (1) The platform name beside \crewModel was hardcoded prose reading "via the OpenAI API"; it is now the generated macro \crewApi, derived from the journal's provenance.provider, so a regenerated table cannot present an archived provider as the current one. (2) The TCB paragraph now states explicitly that prompt and completion content leaves the confidential boundary on every agent call and may be retained by the inference provider under its own abuse-monitoring policy, and that the guarantee is over host-observable shape rather than content. The paper previously said nothing about retention, which understated the scope limit.

Superseded by making the enforced step deadline and the crew model name journal-derived rather than ambient. The deadline-overrun figures were computed against Settings().step_deadline_s, i.e. against whatever TRACEGUARD_STEP_DEADLINE_MS the analysis environment happened to carry -- the same journal reported 12.6% under the 3 s default and would report a different number under the 10 s deadline the live deployment now uses, which is not a reproducible statistic. The value is now recovered from each run's own full-pad rows, whose released per-step duration is the enforced deadline by construction, and surfaced as \stepDeadline. \crewModel likewise stopped being hand-declared-and-warned-about (on a path that returned 0 regardless, so a stale crew name was invisible to CI) and is now generated from provenance.models, naming a heterogeneous crew in full. No reported value changed for the anchored journal: it still measures 12.6% at 3 s and gpt-4o-mini.

Superseded by the completed generality sweep on the Azure confidential-VM deployment: 1152 cells across four spokes plus 288 judged determinations (144 pairs), all against Azure OpenAI. Three of the paper's claims changed, not just its numbers. (1) MEMBERSHIP IS NOW A DETECTED LEAK on the headline crew -- 0.719 against a calibrated null of 0.584 (p<0.0005) where the archived gpt-4o-mini run had 0.566 against 0.569 (p=0.52) and the manuscript reported none. The mechanism is the one that write-up named and dismissed as too small: the canary adds a median +774 B of egress (+9.8%) and +5.0 s while leaving research depth unchanged, against -294 B on the weaker crew. It rides on size (0.710) and timing (0.689) rather than structure (0.591), so structure canonicalization cannot close it and measurably does not (0.665, p=0.0085). Ruled out as artifacts and gated by tests: the two labels are exactly orthogonal (phi=0.000, canary balanced 24/24 per rung) and the canary is byte-identical in length to the distractor it replaces at document, first-sentence and id grain. (2) STRUCTURE CANONICALIZATION RAISES ATTRIBUTE LEAKAGE, 0.763 to 0.845, because removing the data-dependent depth channel leaves fewer but cleaner coordinates to generalize from. (3) THE CREW MODEL DETERMINES WHICH COORDINATE CARRIES THE SECRET: gpt-4o still varies its depth (67% at the public cap, the rest spread from two passes) and leaks the attribute at 0.983, while both gpt-5.6 deployments sit at 95-98% at the cap and fall to 0.747 and 0.774; the pre-declared paired contrast is -0.236 (95% CI [-0.326,-0.139]). Bounded claims: the single-agent ReAct topology clears neither null (p=0.116, p=0.837) because it searches a median two passes against seven; membership is underpowered in every model arm (0.612-0.659 against nulls near 0.62) at half the baseline's runs; the within-sensitive graded trend is indistinguishable from its null, so the ladder answers "sensitive or not" and not "how sensitive"; 9 of 19 Holm hypotheses survive with 3 marginal, resolved at 2000 permutations against the 381 this family requires. Method changes: one estimator throughout (fold mean, pooled emitted alongside) after the headline macros were found mixing them and reversing the ordering of the two secrets; the step deadline and crew model derived from the journal rather than the environment; the depth distribution's shape and the eps-frontier's regime generated rather than asserted, the latter now vacuous because depth saturates; full padding at 120.0 s rather than 36.0 s because the calibrated deadline tripled; and the sweep's design, statistics and mechanism tables moved to a new appendix so the body stays within the 13-page limit.

Installed the in-enclave judged utility run (full-pad 0.549 against a 0.660 baseline, delta 0.111, p=0.003; intact runs 0.66, lost-step runs 0.09; 28/144 fail-closed) and corrected three things it exposed. (1) build() in make_paper_artifacts shadowed the journal with one arm of _records_for output, which drops the condition field, so _enforced_deadline_s found no full-pad rows and fell back to the ambient TRACEGUARD_STEP_DEADLINE_MS: the paper reported a 3 s enforced deadline and a 55.0% overrun rate where the journal shows every padded step at exactly 10.0 s and a 1.0% rate. Re-anchor after correcting the max_tokens objection evidence, the last hand-typed measurement in the body. It claimed no step type came within 95% of its completion cap with "the largest reaching 53%"; 53% is coverage_assessment, while the actual worst case is clinical_extraction at 74% (945 B against a 320-token cap). Adds the wire-level measurement (Appendix D), which closes the soundness gap the adversarial review flagged: the threat model is a host reading the guest NIC while every reported AUC came from the guest runtime own byte counters. Header-only capture at the virtual NIC over 48 sequential undefended runs, packets attributed by partitioning each run timeline using the receipt issued_at for absolute placement. Result: aggregate volume tracks the recorded counters at r=0.993 (request) and r=0.849 (response), and the attribute clears its within-group permutation null on the response direction at the wire (0.742 against 0.578, p=0.011) -- the coordinate Proposition 2 says cannot be padded is the one packet-level measurement confirms. The request direction does not survive as a per-step maximum (0.556, p=0.508) because MTU-scale segmentation quantizes it, though its run total is faithful. Two analysis bugs were found and fixed on the way: overlapping step windows double-counted packets (ingress ratio 6.4x, implausible as TLS overhead) and are replaced by a partition; and a capture filtered only on tcp port 443 collected 227 kB from an unrelated peer, which drove the response correlation to r=-0.04 and would have supported the opposite conclusion. Also fixed every overfull hbox in the document (143pt, 128pt and 14.9pt: two appendix tables widened to table*, and _mc now wraps long footnote rows instead of running 1.8in into the margin).

Adds Figure 4, the wire-level cross-check as a graph: (a) per-run wire bytes against the recorded bytes for both directions, showing the offset from y=x is protocol overhead whose variance, not mean, is what could hide a channel; (b) the attribute recovered per direction at each instrumentation level against the calibrated null, which is where the practical conclusion inverts -- the un-paddable response direction still clears its null on the wire while the closeable request direction drops to chance under MTU segmentation. Also cleared the last overfull hbox and fixed an UnboundLocalError in the figure script that a suppressed stderr had hidden, so an earlier "successful" run had silently reused the previous PDF.

utility.interpretation: Two contrasts against the same baseline, both from the in-enclave judged run (gpt-5.6-terra judge, never a crew model). (1) Structure canonicalization: no detected utility loss -- 0.660 baseline against 0.636 enforced over 140 paired determinations, a difference of 0.023 the paired Wilcoxon test does not distinguish from zero (p=0.67). This is a no-detected-loss result and not an equivalence or non-inferiority claim; a non-significant difference at this sample size bounds the effect loosely. (2) Full padding, the arm the headline (0,0)-on-C claim rests on, IS now separately measured and does cost utility: 0.549 overall against the 0.660 baseline over 141 pairs, a difference of 0.111 (p=0.003). The cost is not a gradual degradation but is mediated entirely by one event -- a step that misses the public deadline is released empty. Padded runs that lost no step score 0.660, matching the baseline exactly, and those that lost one score 0.09; 19% (Wilson 13.8-26.7%) of padded runs lost at least one. The fail-closed rate is a property of the deployment's latency profile rather than of the mechanism: a second enclave measurement of the same condition at the same 10s deadline gave 14.1% (9.8-19.7%), overlapping, while the superseded host-run arm gave 57.6% (49.5-65.4%). The archived gpt-4o-mini crew gave the opposite sign on contrast (1) (enforcement scoring higher, p=0.0035), which its own explanation predicts would vanish here: that crew cut routine cases short so the canonical plan corrected a shortfall, and this crew reaches the extraction cap on nearly every case so there is no shortfall left.

known_limitations: Oblivious retrieval, a confidential GPU, and output differential privacy were assumed/emulated rather than deployed.

The crew ran inside a genuine Azure Confidential VM (AMD SEV-SNP, vTPM, MAA-verified); runs executed with concurrency across cases, which does not affect per-run step ordering but shares host and provider-API load across concurrent runs.

Full-pad latency is real slept wall-clock time: the runtime sleeps each step out to the public deadline, so a full-pad run takes exactly the plan length times the deadline. It is 120.0 s here against 36.0 s on the archived crew; the multiplier over each arm's own baseline is stable (2.2x, 2.3x) and it is the calibrated deadline that tripled, because it must cover the crew's tail latency. That is defensible for an asynchronous back-office workflow and is not an interactive latency.

The full-pad release is (0,0) on the three guest-composed coordinates and is verified as such rather than asserted: across all 192 padded runs the released triple is byte-identical (7-pass canonical plan, every step exactly 10 s and exactly 8192 B). It is NOT (0,0) over the whole observable. The provider-chosen response size cannot be padded (Prop. 2), so the padded arm carries a measured residual there -- membership 0.577 against its calibrated null of 0.58, which it does not clear, and attribute 0.764 against 0.60, which it does. An earlier version of this record claimed a 0.500 full-pad AUC with all released features constant; that was true only of an instrumentation that never recorded the response direction, and it is superseded. The (0,0) statement remains one about the released observable and not proof that an external hardware observer saw an exactly constant trace.

Every reported AUC is a fold mean over held-out (service, topic) groups, read against that arm's own calibrated null (0.58-0.60 here, not 0.50). Pooled values are emitted under a `Pooled` suffix and differ by up to 0.10; the two must not be mixed across the two secrets, which an earlier version of the generator did.

The egress ceiling never binds on this workload, so the size mechanism is provisioned but unexercised and its measured cost is zero. The margin is thinner on this crew than on the archived one, because it writes more.

The depth distribution's shape is model-dependent and is generated rather than asserted: 27% of runs reach the public cap on the archived crew and 97% here, so depth stops discriminating almost entirely. The finite-epsilon template mechanism buckets depth and is therefore vacuous here (97% of runs in one band, 2 of 3 templates ever occupied) -- a low attack AUC at every budget then reflects a near-constant release rather than protection.

Only 2 of the 4 restricted single-coordinate adversaries clear the null on both estimators on this crew (timing, round-trip count), against all 4 on the archived crew. The redundancy claim is real but not uniform, and the difference is the closed depth channel.

The graded ladder answers 'sensitive or not' and not 'how sensitive': the within-sensitive trend is indistinguishable from its null. Sensitivity and documentation-completeness are anti-correlated by construction in this corpus (the top rung's framing is 'documentation absent'), so a ladder holding completeness fixed might recover monotonicity. Flagged as the follow-up rather than claimed.

The autonomy axis is not independent of the defense axis at its bottom rung: scripted control flow *is* a data-independent plan, so 'scripted autonomy' and 'structure canonicalization' name the same intervention. Only the bounded-against-free contrast is clean.

The Holm family reports both secrets on every arm and was widened from the attribute target alone after observing that the two move in opposite directions along the autonomy axis. Widening can only make Holm more conservative, but the membership column of the autonomy row should be read as exploratory rather than confirmatory.
The star design does not identify interactions between factors, and none are claimed. A full crossing at the measured levels would be 81 arms and 7,776 cells against 1,000 completed here.
The model axis is three deployments. That cannot support a scaling law and none is fitted; an ordering and one pre-declared paired contrast are reported instead.

MODEL_* values are Azure *deployment* names, not base-model identifiers, so a redeployment under the same name is a different artifact and the underlying model snapshot is not something the API exposes.

180 cells of the crew-model spoke initially failed on a run-id collision (a truncated identifier collapsed distinct cells) and were re-run after the fix. The journals retain those rows with status 'failed'; every reported count is of completed cells only.

calibrated_nulls.method: Labels permuted within each held-out (service, topic) group, 2000 draws, seed 20260710, re-running the full leave-one-group-out attack per draw. Within-group rather than global so the group-by-label balance the protocol is defined against is preserved.
calibrated_nulls.why_it_matters: The protocol selects the better of two attackers by fold-mean AUC and reports the inversion-safe max(AUC, 1-AUC). Both are attacker-favourable, so the null of the design sits at 0.58-0.60, not 0.50. Every reported AUC is uninterpretable without its own null.
calibrated_nulls.numbers: See calibrated_nulls_measured, which is generated from tables/nulls.json. This block previously carried its own per-arm copy of those numbers and went stale against it; the numbers now have exactly one source.

membership_revision: Reported twice, in opposite directions, and both readings are recorded here. On the archived gpt-4o-mini crew membership was 0.566 against a calibrated null of 0.569 (p=0.52) -- indistinguishable from chance -- and the manuscript reported no detectable membership leak, naming the condition that would overturn it: 'a stronger adversary, a larger corpus, or a canary that perturbs the agent's control flow rather than only its draft length could all expose it'. The gpt-5.6 crew meets that condition through draft length, the mechanism the earlier write-up identified and dismissed as too small: membership is 0.719 against 0.584 (p<0.0005), the canary adding a median +774 B of egress (+9.8%) and +5.0 s of wall time while leaving research depth unchanged, where the same measurement on the weaker crew gives -294 B, i.e. noise. Ruled out as artifacts, both gated by tests: the two labels are exactly orthogonal by construction (phi=0.000, canary balanced 24/24 at every sensitivity rung), and the canary is byte-identical in length to the distractor it replaces at whole-document, first-sentence and document-id grain. The leak rides on size (0.710) and timing (0.689) rather than structure (0.591), so structure canonicalization cannot close it and measurably does not (0.665, p=0.0085). The claim the manuscript now makes is that trace leakage is a property of the agent's competence and not only of its architecture, which is uncomfortable for any defense validated once and then trusted across model upgrades.

frontier_partition.finding: Residual leakage at large epsilon depends on the public template partition, and a partition that isolates the routine mode in a band of its own gives attribute AUC 0.96 at eps=8 -- above the undefended fold-mean of 0.784. A coarser noised release leaking more than the full trace is not a contradiction: the released template is one clean categorical, while the undefended attacker must generalize a twenty-feature vector across a held-out task group. All partitions converge on the calibrated null as epsilon shrinks, so it is the high-utility end of the frontier that is partition sensitive.
frontier_partition.published_partition: equal bands over the published CANON-v1 depth range [2, 7] -> [3.67, 5.33]
frontier_partition.superseded_partition: empirical tertiles, which collapsed to [3.0, 3.0] and occupied 2 of 3 templates

reproducible_build: The manuscript builds byte-identically from identical source: pdfTeX otherwise stamps /CreationDate, /ModDate and a random /ID into the trailer, which repeatedly invalidated this anchor and made "the PDF changed" indistinguishable from "a number changed". The \pdfinfoomitdate, \pdftrailerid and \pdfsuppressptexinfo directives in the preamble are sufficient on their own: a build with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH unset and TZ=Asia/Kolkata reproduces the same SHA-256 as `make paper`, so the anchor is environment-independent and not merely stable under one recipe. Verified over five clean rebuilds plus that cross-environment check. Rebuild with `make paper`.
provider_migration: Paper claims are moving from the archived direct-OpenAI journals to live Azure OpenAI runs. \crewModel and \crewApi are both generated from the journal that produced the numbers, so the manuscript names the platform it actually ran on; while the anchored tables still derive from artifacts/experiment-usenix26-main.jsonl they correctly read gpt-4o-mini via the OpenAI API, labelled historical in source.paper_models.
deadline_provenance: The step deadline is a calibrated deployment parameter, not a constant: measured p50 3.0 s / p99 8.7 s on the gpt-5.6 Azure deployments means the published 3 s value would fail closed on 48.3% of steps, so production runs at 10 s. Because the overrun figures depend on it, the analysis recovers the deadline from the journal's own padded traces and refuses to average across a journal that spans two deadlines; a journal with no padded rows makes the analysis warn and label the figures provisional rather than quietly using the reader's environment.
